subject: Write and run the Ljung-Box residual test -- decision gate G1
description:
THE PLAN'S NAMED GATE (task_plan.md G1). No Ljung-Box code existed anywhere in the repo -- verified by repo-wide grep. It was written from scratch as 01_SRQ1_Model_Training/02_thesis_modelling/model_training/srq1/srq1_residual_diagnostics.py (GREEN zone, purely additive).

SCOPE CORRECTION MADE BEFORE CODING: this task originally said to read the four persisted models AND pass dof = p+q. Those describe different models -- p and q are ARIMA orders, while the persisted artefacts are XGBoost/LightGBM, which have neither. Brian chose ARIMA-only. Consequence: no persisted model is read, nothing is retrained, and no Branch A artefact is touched. SARIMAX refits from the matrix in seconds.

Design: fits the same SARIMAX(1,1,1) as the reported baseline, on the same series under the same retention rule, tests at lag 24 (2m, m=12) with dof = p+q = 2 derived from ARIMA_ORDER rather than typed.

VERDICT -- G1 PASSED 2026-09-13: AUTOCORRELATION REMAINS, so the 2.B feature additions are justified.
  51/230 series reject at alpha=0.05 = 22.2%, vs ~5% expected under white noise (4.4x chance), WITH the 9.7 correction applied.
  Rejecting brands: median ACF(12) = +0.361. Non-rejecting: +0.064. A 5.6x separation at exactly the seasonal lag -- the remaining structure is ANNUAL.
  29 of the 35 brands exceeding their own 2/sqrt(n) band at lag 12 also reject Ljung-Box.
  Only 5/230 SARIMAX fits (2.2%) failed to converge -- far too few to explain the rate.

SECOND OUTCOME: this is also the evidence for task 8 (repair 2.A1). A non-seasonal ARIMA on monthly beverage demand leaving annual autocorrelation in a quarter of its series demonstrates the seasonal-order defect rather than asserting it.

Outputs (all NEW, no existing table regenerated): 05_thesis_results/05_model_benchmark/tables/residual_diagnostics.{md,csv} and residual_diagnostics_per_brand.csv

Cost: free. No retrain, no API spend.
